headline: FFWC warns of flash floods in 10 districts within 48 hours
summary: Heavy rainfall in Bangladesh and upstream Indian states has caused major rivers to rise, threatening low-lying areas across the north and northeast.
details: The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) has issued a special outlook warning that short-term and flash floods could hit at least ten districts in the northern and northeastern regions within the next 24 to 48 hours.
Heavy rainfall inside Bangladesh and across upstream Indian states, including Assam, Meghalaya, and West Bengal, has caused a rapid rise in major river levels.
Currently, the Kushiyara river is flowing above danger marks at Chhatak and Fenchuganj in Sylhet, while the Someshwari river has breached its danger limit in Netrokona, inundating low-lying areas.
Water levels of the Surma and Kushiyara are projected to swell further over the next three days, worsening conditions in Sylhet and Sunamganj.

In the north and northwest, the Teesta, Dharla, and Dudhkumar rivers are rising significantly, with the Teesta already at warning levels. These rivers may cross danger marks within 48 hours, risking flash floods in Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari, Rangpur, Gaibandha, and Kurigram.

The Brahmaputra-Jamuna river system is also on a steady upward trend and is expected to reach warning limits within 24 to 72 hours, threatening regions in Kurigram, Gaibandha, Jamalpur, Bogura, Sirajganj, and Tangail.
In Rajshahi division, the Atrai and Chhoto Jamuna rivers are projected to temporarily submerge low-lying areas in Naogaon and Natore within three days.

FFWC Executive Engineer Sardar Udoy Raihan confirmed the risk for low-lying areas in Rangpur, Rajshahi, Sylhet, and Mymensingh divisions, though he assured there is no possibility of major or prolonged flooding at this time.

headline: Madrasa principal arrested for sexually assaulting 12-year-old student
summary: The accused was detained by locals and handed over to police in Lakshmipur after the victim fled the institution and informed his mother.
details: Police have arrested Abdul Ahad, 46, the principal of Popular Ideal Hifz Madrasa in Lakshmipur's Chandraganj upazila, on allegations of sexually assaulting a 12-year-old student.
According to police, Ahad allegedly called the student to his room on Saturday night and assaulted him. The boy fled the madrasa the following afternoon and returned home to inform his mother.
The victim's mother brought the matter to the attention of local residents and guardians, who then went to the madrasa, detained the accused and handed him over to the police.

The principal was produced before a court this afternoon, where the judge ordered him to be sent to jail. An investigation into the incident is ongoing, and the child has been sent to the hospital for a medical examination.
caption:
A madrasa principal in Lakshmipur has been arrested after a 12-year-old student accused him of sexual assault.

Police have arrested Abdul Ahad, 46, the principal of Popular Ideal Hifz Madrasa in Lakshmipur's Chandraganj upazila, on allegations of sexually assaulting a 12-year-old student.

According to police, Ahad allegedly called the student to his room on Saturday night and assaulted him. The boy fled the madrasa the following afternoon and returned home to inform his mother.

The victim's mother brought the matter to the attention of local residents and guardians, who then went to the madrasa, detained the accused and handed him over to the police.

The principal was produced before a court this afternoon, where the judge ordered him to be sent to jail. An investigation into the incident is ongoing, and the child has been sent to the hospital for a medical examination.
